stories.headline: Front Range Passenger Rail District names former Jefferson County clerk as election official after ballot error
stories.summary:
The Front Range Passenger Rail District board voted unanimously Monday night to name Pam Anderson, a former Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder, as its designated election official for Ballot Issue 7A, effective immediately. The move came almost two weeks after the district announced that about 800,000 Colorado voters would receive ballots that wrongly include the sales tax question.

The question was printed on ballots in Adams, Arapahoe, Douglas and Weld counties even though voters there are not eligible to vote on it. State and county officials have said the district failed to tell county clerks about its updated boundaries after the legislature shrank its footprint in a 2026 law. The previous election official and attorney, Brent Butzin, resigned Oct. 12.

Issue 7A is a .333% sales tax increase to expand the rail line from Denver to Pueblo. Election officials have said clerks can still count votes accurately. Anderson told the board that county clerks can block tabulated results for ineligible voters, and that the process includes a public audit and canvass.

stories.headline: RTD board candidates cite budget deficit, public trust and short terms as five seats go to voters
stories.summary:
Metro Denver voters will elect five new members to the Regional Transportation District board in November. The incoming directors face an ongoing deficit, a new chief executive officer, route cuts and a possible 2028 ballot measure to raise funding.

Under a new state law, the 15-member elected board will shrink to nine members starting in 2029, and only five will be chosen by voters. The new governor will appoint the other four, subject to Senate confirmation. Six candidates are competing for three contested seats.

Candidates told The Denver Post that the budget, lack of public trust and serving a district of more than 2,000 square miles are top concerns. District K candidate Michael Farrington pointed to the delayed BroncosRide as an example of overpromising. Candidate Jessica Sandgren said she does not support RTD funding Front Range Passenger Rail, while most others said they do.

stories.headline: Bow Mar approves Sheridan Boulevard gate contract; Denver weighs retaliatory gate
stories.summary:
Leaders of the town of Bow Mar gave final approval Monday to a contract for a controlled-access gate on South Sheridan Boulevard. The gate is meant to stop cut-through traffic and is expected to be in place by Thanksgiving, though it will not operate until January. The town also approved a permanent closure of West Tufts Avenue at the town line.

Denver City Councilman Kevin Flynn called the decision an unacceptable alteration of Denver's right of way. He said Denver is considering a "nuclear option": its own limited-access gate just north of Bow Mar's, which would block residents from reaching the town from the north. He said his constituents would lose access to the traffic signal at Sheridan and Quincy.

Bow Mar says about 1,200 vehicles enter via Sheridan daily, up 51% in eight years, and that police have issued nearly 900 citations in four years. A vehicle was recently found partially submerged in Bowles Lake. Denver and Littleton had jointly asked the town to halt the project.

stories.headline: Man arrested after road rage leads to shooting at Aurora school pickup
stories.summary:
A 35-year-old family member of an Aurora high school student was arrested Tuesday after he allegedly fired a gun during student pickup. Police said the incident stemmed from a road rage argument.

Aurora police did not publicly identify the man, who had been arguing with another person at the time of the shooting.

The incident occurred at a school pickup area while students were being picked up. Further details on injuries and charges were not immediately available.

stories.headline: RedPeak buys Cheesman Park's Manchester apartments for $23 million
stories.summary:
Local apartment investor RedPeak paid $23 million last week for The Manchester, a 14-story, 100-unit building near Cheesman Park and the Denver Botanic Gardens. Built in 1973, it sold for the first time, bought from members of the original investor group that had owned it since the mid-1970s.

The price works out to $230,000 per unit, which RedPeak chief investment officer Craig Kalman said is less than half the cost of building it today. The building has mostly one- and two-bedroom units, a gym, community room and indoor pool. RedPeak plans to renovate it and owns five other buildings in the city.

Kalman noted that multifamily values are down 20% to 30% nationally. CBRE reported $386 million in Denver apartment sales in the second quarter of 2026, down from $681 million a year earlier, with average price per unit down 22% to $236,000. He said he expects Denver to come back stronger.

stories.headline: Defense agency awards record research contract to CU Anschutz medical campus
stories.summary:
The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency has awarded a research contract to the Aurora medical campus at CU Anschutz. The Denver Business Journal reported the funding is the most ever awarded in a federal contract at the campus.

The award is intended to produce both military and civilian benefits. The report's URL indicates the research concerns blood.

Further details on the amount and scope of the work were not available in the preview of the article.

stories.headline: Broncos at 4-2 face Cardinals as national rankings question Bo Nix's play
stories.summary:
The Broncos improved to 4-2 with an overtime win over Seattle, secured when Wil Lutz kicked a 53-yard field goal after a Ja'Quan McMillian interception. The defense sacked Sam Darnold five times and intercepted him twice.

Quarterback Bo Nix completed 17 of 27 passes for 107 yards, and national analysts have questioned his play. Coach Sean Payton has stayed supportive, and has taken playcalling duties from Davis Webb after four games.

Denver visits the Arizona Cardinals (2-4) at 2:05 p.m. Sunday. National power rankings praise the defense and the quality of the Broncos' wins while criticizing the offense and run game.

stories.headline: Colorado's Deion Sanders says 'don't count me out' after 2-4 start
stories.summary:
Colorado head coach Deion Sanders said people should not count him out despite the Buffaloes' 2-4 start to the season.

Colorado played Utah on Saturday, Oct. 17, in Boulder, where offensive lineman Jayven Richardson was helped off the field after an injury in the first half.

The Denver Gazette reported on Sanders' comments on Tuesday as the team looks to rebound.

stories.headline: Avalanche fall to Devils 4-3, drop to 5-4-1
stories.summary:
The Colorado Avalanche lost to the New Jersey Devils 4-3 on Tuesday, Oct. 20. The result left Colorado at 5-4-1, fourth in the Central Division and seventh in the Western Conference.

New Jersey improved to 5-4-0, fifth in the Metropolitan Division.

The game aired on KTVD Channel 20, where Denver-area viewers can watch Nuggets and Avalanche games free over the air with a digital antenna.

topStory.headline: Russia Frees Retired American Teacher Stephen Hubbard as Trump Envoy Witkoff Meets Putin in St. Petersburg
topStory.summary:
Russia has released Stephen Hubbard, a 74-year-old retired teacher from Michigan who had been detained in Ukraine in 2022, as U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff held talks with President Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday. Hubbard had been held on charges, which he denies, of fighting as a mercenary in Ukraine, and he was the last American designated by the State Department as wrongfully detained in Russia. In remarks aired on Russian state news agencies, Putin said Hubbard was at the airport, and the Kremlin described the release as a goodwill gesture.

Witkoff praised Putin during the meeting, saying, "You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian. You are a humanitarian also, sir." President Donald Trump said on Truth Social that Hubbard was on his way home and that the United States "was not required to give anything in return." Trump said he had asked Putin directly for the release in a phone call last week. Hubbard's family thanked Trump and his team for opening a dialogue with Russia. Witkoff told Putin that "groundwork" had been laid for ending the fighting, said he had brought documents outlining possible approaches to a deal, and expressed hope that Russia would consider resuming trilateral talks. Jared Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, was expected to join the meeting virtually.

The meeting followed talks on Tuesday in Oslo, where Witkoff and other U.S. negotiators met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, European leaders, and the leaders of Norway and Finland. A U.S. official described the talks as "very productive and constructive," with "strong alignment at the working level" on next steps, and told NBC News that Ukraine brought forward new proposals. Finnish President Alexander Stubb said "genuine progress" had been made but cautioned that patience would be needed. Zelenskyy said a possible trilateral leaders' meeting was among the important ideas raised. He also said U.S. intelligence sharing, including early warning of ballistic missile attacks, "works now" after Kyiv had accused Washington of withholding it, a claim the U.S. called "scandalous."

The diplomacy comes as relations between Washington and Kyiv have deteriorated in recent weeks. Trump has said it is time for Ukraine to get a new president or for "somebody else to negotiate on behalf of Ukraine," and on Tuesday he told reporters, "We want Zelenskyy to make a deal." His administration has also waived sanctions on Russia and agreed to a diesel deal with the Kremlin, moves that have drawn criticism at home and abroad. Trump has also blamed Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries for rising fuel prices, which have climbed since the start of the U.S.-led war on Iran, ahead of next month's midterm elections.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said the Kremlin would listen to what Witkoff offered but ruled out "any political concessions." Russia controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory, and its drone attacks continued this week. Ukrainian officials said at least 10 people were killed on Tuesday in Kyiv and its region, Donetsk and Dnipro, and two more were killed near Kharkiv overnight into Wednesday. Zelenskyy and European allies have said it is now up to Russia to respond to the proposals agreed in Oslo, and the outcome of the St. Petersburg talks will help determine whether trilateral negotiations resume.
